Omar Ruiz: Heads up 1 I accepted an external offer and my last day will be June 18 (mid-pay-period). I have an outstanding 401(k) loan and I9m enrolled in family HDHP HSA. Questions: what happens to the loan balance at separation? Can I rollover the 401(k) and keep my HSA contributions if I move to a non-HSA employer midyear?

Kaitlyn Wu: Congrats on the new role! Short: loans at separation usually must be repaid or are treated as a taxable distribution if not repaid within plan rules. HSA contributions from Redwood stop at final payroll. HSA account stays with you; you can continue contributing via bank transfer.

Tara (Benefits Ops): Adding details: 1) 401(k) loan: plan doc requires repayment on separation or it's declared a default/distribution. We offer two paths: immediate payoff via loan offset (taxable distribution) OR continue repayments via direct ACH to recordkeeper if plan admin approves. Let us know which you prefer and we9ll initiate the paperwork.

Omar Ruiz: If it becomes a taxable distribution, will I get a 1099-R for that year? Any early-withdrawal penalties apply?

Tara (Benefits Ops): Yes, if the loan is treated as a deemed distribution you9ll receive a 1099-R and it may be subject to income tax and a 10% early withdrawal penalty if you are under 591/2, unless an exception applies. We will provide the distribution code used. You can avoid the taxable event by rolling the distribution into an IRA within 60 days, but that only applies to actual distributions (you must receive and rollover funds). If you want to avoid distribution entirely, request ACH repayment option before final payroll.

PayrollBot: Automated: "Final paycheck will include any eligible accrued pay. 401(k) loan offsets and final deferrals are processed per plan instruction. Employees should confirm final paycheck with payroll@redwood.com."

Omar Ruiz: About the HSA 1 I switch to a new employer with individual coverage starting July 1. I was on family coverage at Redwood through June 18. Can I still contribute up to family limit for months I was on family plan? Is there a last-month rule here?

Kaitlyn Wu: You get HSA contribution limits based on your coverage status per month. If you had family HDHP coverage for part of the year, you can contribute for those months up to family prorated amount. The "last-month rule" only applies if you9re HSA-eligible on Dec 1 and you stay eligible the following 12 months; looks like that won9t apply here since you9re leaving midyear.

Tara (Benefits Ops): Practical steps: 1) We will stop payroll HSA deferrals at your final paycheck. 2) You retain the HSA account and can contribute after-tax directly to your HSA bank. 3) If you want to maximize family-limit months before departure, we can calculate prorated limits; email benefits@redwood.com with your exact coverage dates and we9ll confirm numbers.

Omar Ruiz: For the loan ACH option, how long does approval take? I9d rather not trigger a distribution if possible.

Tara (Benefits Ops): ACH approval usually takes 5-10 business days to set up + reconciliation with the recordkeeper. Because your separation is imminent, please email benefits@redwood.com today and we9ll prioritize. If ACH can9t be set up before final payroll, we will discuss options (e.g., short-term payroll withholding or documented repayment plan).

hr-bot: Policy note: "On separation, outstanding loan balances are subject to plan provisions. Employer-sponsored HSA payroll deductions end with final pay; HSAs remain owned by the participant. Contact benefits@redwood.com for separation-specific assistance."

Omar Ruiz: Thanks everyone 1 I9ll email benefits now and copy payroll. Appreciate the quick steps.
